messages:
liam_support: customer reports invoice >> dashboard discrepancy for embeddings. invoice shows 12,480 units but dashboard shows ~8,320 for same period. customer id acct-7421, sample request id req-99c3b.

jordan_eng: can you paste the raw request payload & the header info (model, batch size, idempotency-key)?

liam_support: here's the sanitized curl they sent:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: " \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-001","inputs": ["short text A", "..." /* ~500 items*/] }'
```

They said batches were ~500 items, many small. request timestamp: 2026-02-15T14:33:19Z. No Idempotency-Key set.

maria_billing: ok can you share the billing log for req-99c3b? looking for billing_event ids and any duplicate markers.

liam_support: pasted billing log extract:

```
billing_event: be-20260215-01 req=req-99c3b items=500 accounted_tokens=12480 duplicate=false
billing_event: be-20260215-02 req=req-99c3b items=500 accounted_tokens=12480 duplicate=true
```

nodea_sre: I see a pattern — two billing events for same client request. earlier bug (BILL-412) allowed partial-success fallback to emit a second billing event when batch split + retry happened. if the SDK doesn't provide idempotency-key, server retries can generate a second bill.

liam_support: customer insists they only made one call. they used the official SDK but on an older pinned version.

jordan_eng: can reproduce locally with a script that opens two parallel connections and triggers batch-splitting. share repro script pls.

liam_support: repro steps below (short):
1) send one POST with 500 inputs in a single connection without idempotency-key
2) simulate transient 503 mid-body from LB (we used tcpkill)
3) client retries the whole request; server accepted both fragments and billing pipeline emitted two events due to missing dedupe key

python snippet:

```python
# simplified repro
import requests
payload = {"model":"text-embed-001","inputs":["x"]*500}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json=payload, timeout=5)
print(resp.status_code)
```

tim_bot: [ingest-billing-bot] billing_event(be-20260215-01) duplicate_flag=true — noted by pipeline

maria_billing: confirmed: two billing events tied to the same trace id. looks like pipeline uses request_id for dedupe, but when a retry arrives a new internal billing_event id is emitted. the fix: include idempotency-key in billing dedupe key (batch_id or Idempotency-Key header). I'll open a ticket to credit customer.

nodea_sre: mitigation: add default non-empty Idempotency-Key in SDK (v2.4.1) and backfill dedupe for last 14 days using trace_id grouping.

jordan_eng: I'll make the SDK change + add server-side check to drop duplicate billing events if body_checksum + client_ip + model match within 2m window. opening PR now.

liam_support: thanks — can we send the customer a credit and an explanation? suggested msg: "We found a rare edge case where retries without an idempotency key could double-bill batched embedding requests. We're issuing a credit and deploying a fix; please upgrade SDK v2.4.1 when available."

maria_billing: agreed. I'll issue a pro-rated credit and attach reconciliation CSV.

jordan_eng: follow-up: we also saw rerank calls chained to embeddings in their app; confirm that rerank requests don't cause a recompute of the same embeddings (they don't currently), so the extra bill solely came from duplicate embedding billing events.

liam_support: customer notified. closing thread after hotfix. :thumbsup:
